previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A patient with a history of refractory bipolar disorder, depression, and prior suicide attempts was admitted after a suicide attempt involving an intentional overdose of tramadol and Phenergan. She self-presented to the ED after an argument with her mother, whom she cares for. In the ED, she had a brief episode of hypoxia and reduced responsiveness, responded to Narcan, and was stabilized. She was monitored for 48 hours without complications. A CT head showed no acute abnormalities. Her psychiatric medications were adjusted, with quetiapine reduced to 150mg nightly and a PRN dose added for agitation. Tramadol was discontinued due to its risk in mood disorders and substance use history. She was medically cleared and discharged to an inpatient psychiatric facility for ECT. Chronic conditions including hypothyroidism and GERD were managed with continued levothyroxine and ranitidine. The patient expressed ongoing chronic pelvic pain from endometriosis but committed to avoiding opioid dependence. Social stressors related to caregiving were acknowledged, and support services were recommended.
